clue.text: Eat away at fuel element in heart of reactor

indicators.note: the fuel element is placed in the reactor's heart, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the core is the central part of a nuclear reactor
a fuel rod is the element holding nuclear fuel in a reactor

explanation.surface: A warning about something gnawing at a fuel component deep inside a nuclear reactor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' tempts a solver to take the middle letter of 'reactor'; here the phrase is a plain synonym for the reactor's central part, and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to corrode is to wear something away gradually, as rust or acid does to metal.

clue.text: Immature animal eats everything

indicators.note: the animal swallows the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a cow is an animal
all means everything

explanation.surface: A young beast with a big appetite devours everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: callow describes someone young and inexperienced, green.

clue.text: Cad runs over appealing carnivore

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the runs letter above the carnivore

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the otter is a meat-eating animal widely thought cute

explanation.surface: A cad drives over a cute animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rotter is an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel or bounder.

clue.text: Alien hiding in public dance is lacking restraint

parts.note: overt means done in public, open

indicators.note: the alien hides inside the dance, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial lurking at a public dance behaves wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something over the top is excessive, beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Blunder has rascal guillotined

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a terror is a mischievous child, a rascal

explanation.surface: A mistake: the little rascal has been executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blunder is a mistake.

clue.text: Judge a royal nipper

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy
something that nips is a biter

explanation.surface: A royal child, a little nipper, sits in judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like British slang for a small child, but here it is literally one who nips: a BITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an arbiter is someone who settles disputes, a judge or referee.

clue.text: Place trap carelessly and this could be upset

indicators.note: carelessly says the letters are arranged haphazardly

explanation.surface: A clumsily set trap may knock something over.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to upset the applecart is to spoil a plan, so the cart is the thing upset.

clue.text: Worker gets king a drink

parts.note: a worker is a kind of bee
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An employee fetches the king a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: beer is a common alcoholic drink brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Youth to generate transformation

indicators.note: a transformation reshapes the letters of the word generate into another order

explanation.surface: A young person working to bring about change.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a youth is a young person, someone in their teens.

clue.text: Hard-hearted? Girl not so much!

parts.note: Ruth is a girl's name
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Is she cruel? The girl is less so.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ruthless means pitiless, without compassion.

clue.text: Turner is delayed about an hour

indicators.note: the word for delayed goes around the hour, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: delayed means late
H is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Someone named Turner is running about an hour late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like a person's name or the painter; it is a machine that turns wood or metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe spins a workpiece so it can be shaped, so it is literally a thing that turns.

clue.text: Theatre company dislike picture

parts.note: REP is short for repertory, a theatre company
to resent is to dislike bitterly

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe takes against a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to picture something and to represent it both mean to depict or portray it.

clue.text: Open vessel journalist upset

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a vessel or vase
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist is openly distressed about a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something upset has been knocked over, tipped on its side.

clue.text: Greet bad weather

definitions.meaning: to call out a greeting to them
frozen rain falling as pellets of ice

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb of greeting and a noun for falling ice pellets.

clue.text: He attracts constituents but only with difficulty

indicators.note: constituents are the parts that make something up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A politician draws voters, but it is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters in a constituency; it signals rearranging the component letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: done at a stretch means managed only by straining, with difficulty.

clue.text: Siren in car sent hens crazy

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of these three words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A seductive woman in a car drives the chickens wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Sirens lured sailors with song; any alluring, captivating woman can be called one.

clue.text: God's in charge of working animal

indicators.note: the god's name sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: care means charge, as in in someone's care
Thor is the Norse god of thunder, so THOR'S

explanation.surface: A god is put in charge of a beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a carthorse is a heavy horse bred for pulling carts and ploughs.

clue.text: Utter nothing in between

indicators.note: nothing goes into the word for between

parts.note: through can mean between, as in Monday through Friday
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Say nothing in the meantime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like the verb to speak; it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: utter and thorough both mean complete, absolute, as in an utter or thorough mess.

clue.text: Superior reduced strike

parts.note: upper means higher, superior
cut means reduced, as in cut prices

explanation.surface: A boss reduces strike action.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an uppercut is a boxing blow struck upward to the chin.

clue.text: Trendy Italian banker boxes celebrated doctor

parts.note: hip means fashionable, trendy
a banker is something with banks, a river; the Po is Italy's longest
crates are boxes

explanation.surface: A fashionable Italian bank manager punches a famous physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests finance, but in crosswords it is a river; 'boxes' is a noun, not the verb to punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Greek physician of antiquity, often called the father of medicine, behind the doctors' oath.

clue.text: Stick semi-digested food with jelly

parts.note: cud is the part-digested food a cow chews again
a gel is a jelly

explanation.surface: Glue together half-chewed food with jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the verb to glue; it is the noun, a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short thick stick used as a weapon.

clue.text: Model wearing fewer clothes?

parts.note: having fewer clothes is having less of them
on means being worn, as in what you have on

explanation.surface: A fashion model wearing less than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LESS ON, the answer says wearing fewer clothes; the question mark flags this play.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a model or example to learn from, as in let that be a lesson.

clue.text: Look suggestively back in the dance

indicators.note: back says the word for looking suggestively is read from the end to the start

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone suggestively

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a partner lewdly from the back of the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp has time to recycle liqueur

parts.note: Mrs Mopp was the charlady in the old BBC radio comedy ITMA, so a char or cleaner
to recycle is to reuse

explanation.surface: The cleaner finds a moment to recycle the liqueur bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is a British cleaning lady; Mrs Mopp, from the wartime radio show ITMA, is the classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a French herbal liqueur, green or yellow, first made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Travel across German mountain range

indicators.note: the travelling word goes across, around, the German letter

parts.note: to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: Journeying over a range of German mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow chain of hills or mountain crests.

clue.text: Jacob's wife finds the meadow hot

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Jacob's wife discovers the field is warm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob married two sisters, Leah first and then Rachel.

clue.text: Relative gets a halt signal that's not vindicated

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
a red light signals traffic to halt

explanation.surface: A family member is stopped by a red light and the charge stands against him.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose name has not been cleared remains under suspicion, not shown to be innocent.

clue.text: Children's game gets you and me in river

parts.note: tag is a chasing game played by children
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Kids playing tag together in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, flowing out at Lisbon.

clue.text: Camera socket stolen by son with long-handled instrument

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a hoe is a long-handled garden tool

explanation.surface: A camera part goes missing, along with a son and a garden tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshoe is the bracket on top of a camera into which a flashgun slots and makes contact.

clue.text: Part of the creche longs for rank

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sentence about what a nursery longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for rank' as the definition; 'for' is a link word joining wordplay to definition, and only 'rank' can stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or grade in an organisation, a rank in its hierarchy.
